prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Hi, I am looking for any kind of wine that is not too heavy and goes down really easily, and I want to spend between 20 and 40 euros."

List A:
Wine 1: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $15. Tasting note: "Here's a wine that will surprise you. It has real richness and varietal flavor, and is dry and balanced, with the weight you want in a nice Cabernet. Might even get a little better in another year or two."
Wine 2: Syrah, US, $12. Tasting note: "Here's a dry, somewhat brawny wine that has some charm. It's filled with briary, peppery flavors, with fruits suggesting blackberries and cassis. Good value in an inexpensive steak and chops wine."
Wine 3: Tempranillo, Spain, $21. Tasting note: "More sharp and jumpy than many over-$20 wines from the region, but if you like a more racy, acidic style it may be up your alley. The wine offers blackberry flavors, spice and some herbal notes, while the finish thickens with mushroom and chocolate. A good but sketchy wine with a few loose ends."
Wine 4: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $7. Tasting note: "Here's a wine you can serve your guests at a big party and not have to worry about price. It's dry and fruity enough to work with anything calling for a robust red wine."
Wine 5: Red Blend, US, $17. Tasting note: "An affordably priced wine brings meaty, peppery aromas, interesting fruit, spice and smoke flavors, and a mouthcoating texture. It is full bodied, complex and concentrated."

List B:
Wine 1: Pinot Noir, US, $20. Tasting note: "A pretty good Pinot that, at the equivalent of 10 bucks a bottle, is a nice buy. It's an easy wine, dry, light-bodied and silky, with modest cherry and spice flavors."
Wine 2: Pinot Noir, US, $18. Tasting note: "Don't discount this Pinot Noir because it's in a screw top and the price is under $20. It's quite a nice wine, dry and silky. Made in a lighter style to be opened now, it has pleasant cherry, cola and sandalwood flavors."
Wine 3: Pinot Noir, US, $8. Tasting note: "Weird name, simple wine, but not a bad one. It's awfully hard to get distinction in Pinot Noir at this price. The wine is dry, and there are some berry flavors wrapped in silky tannins."
Wine 4: Pinot Grigio, US, $11. Tasting note: "This wine's citrus, apple, floral and vanilla flavors are dryish to off-dry. It's a soft, simple wine that will appeal to folks who like a little sweetness in the finish."
Wine 5: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $15. Tasting note: "Here's a wine that will surprise you. It has real richness and varietal flavor, and is dry and balanced, with the weight you want in a nice Cabernet. Might even get a little better in another year or two."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
